record.original_question: Define and study symmetry for random strings and random sequences. Is lack of symmetry a sign of non-randomness?

evidence.quote: Define and study the symmetry of random strings and sequences. Is the absence of symmetry a symptom of non-randomness? (C. Calude)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the setting of algorithmic information theory. For a finite binary string $x \in \{0,1\}^*$, let $K(x)$ denote its prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity. Call a string $x$ of length $n$ (Kolmogorov-)random if $K(x) \ge n - O(1)$, and call an infinite binary sequence $X \in \{0,1\}^\omega$ (Martin-Löf) random if there is a constant $c$ such that $K(X\!\upharpoonright\!n) \ge n - c$ for all $n$.

Introduce a general notion of "symmetry" for finite strings and infinite sequences. By a symmetry of a string $x$ of length $n$ one may understand, for instance, a nontrivial permutation $\sigma \in S_n$ such that $x_{\sigma(i)} = x_i$ for all $i$, or more generally invariance of $x$ under some structured family of transformations (reflections, rotations, block permutations, affine maps on indices, etc.); analogous definitions can be formulated for infinite sequences via shift-, reflection-, or block-invariances on initial segments.

The problem is twofold:

(a) Propose a mathematically robust definition of symmetry (and of a quantitative measure of symmetry, e.g.\ the size or descriptive complexity of the group of symmetries of $x$) for random finite strings and for random infinite sequences.

(b) Under such a definition, determine whether the absence of symmetry is a necessary feature of randomness. Specifically: is it true that every Kolmogorov-random string, respectively every Martin-Löf random infinite sequence, has only trivial symmetries (in the proposed sense), and conversely does the presence of nontrivial symmetry imply a quantifiable defect in randomness (e.g.\ a bound $K(x) \le n - f(x)$ where $f(x)$ grows with the amount of symmetry)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in algorithmic information theory attributed to C. Calude. No published resolution defining symmetry for random strings/sequences and establishing the symmetry/non-randomness equivalence appears in standard sources; the problem remains open.
